title: Monmouth County home among America's most haunted. Learn more
excerpt: Looking for real ghost stories? A historic tavern in Port Monmouth tops the list of New Jersey's most haunted places to visit.
content:
Oct. 10, 2026, 4:55 a.m. ET

Ready to scream your way into the spooky season?

According to a report by HouseBeautiful.com, there are haunted houses across the U.S. that have spine-chilling tales that will send shivers down to your toes.

The online interior decorating magazine list of creepy homes distinct backstory, but all have hosted many creepy, unexplainable occurrences — including disembodied sounds, eerie touches, sudden movements and more odd happenings, the report stated.

Thrill seekers on a mission for a scary night can visit these top haunts that consists of grand mansions, historic farmhouses and light houses that have all had endless reports of ghost sightings.

For New Jersey, the writer's chose a location in Monmouth County.

Spy House, Port Monmouth: No. 29

Nicknamed the "Spy House," this historic site dates back to 1663 and was famously used as a tavern during the Revolutionary War. Ghost sightings include a "woman in white," mysterious sobbing noises, and a sea captain.

According to newjerseyhauntedhouses.com it was dubbed the "Spy House" due to workers over hearing British troops plans and relayed their discussions to colonial troops.

Also known as the Seabrook-Wilson House, it is on the National Register of Historic Places and is part of the Monmouth County Park System. The Park System acquired the house in 1998 from Middletown Township and it has since been fully restored. The house serves as the Bayshore Waterfront Park Activity Center, according to Monmouth County Park System.

Haunted houses in the Mid-Atlantic region

According to House Beautiful, these states haunted houses have a chilling back stories steeped in historic tales. Below are haunted housse in the Tri-State worthy of a spooky visit. Here's what writer's said about each location.

New London Ledge Lighthouse, Groton, CT: No. 7

If you prefer your haunts on dry land, make sure to visit Connecticut's ghost town. This home has been featured on several ghost-hunting shows. There seems to be only one spirit here named "Ernie"— the former residence of several lighthouse keepers, but he's got a very strong presence. He likes to turn televisions off and on, take sheets off beds, and generally cause a ruckus by knocking.

Woodburn Mansion, Dover, DE: No. 8

Known for an active site of ghostly encounters, this stately Georgian home was built in 1790. Allegedly, a mysterious little girl who appeared floating in a fountain at a 1985 inauguration to the boisterous Revolutionary soldiers who allegedly drink any wine left out haunts it. In 1965 it was purchased by the state to use as a governor's residence.

'The Death House,' New York City, NY: No. 31

This 19th-century brownstone has been the site of several unexplained deaths and violence. Apparently, Mark Twain is said to lurk around here sporting a handsome white linen suit. This Greenwich Village brownstone along West 10th Street is known for paranormal activity, especially from previous tenants.

Baker Mansion, Altoona, PA: No. 37

Built in the 1840s, the home's original residents are said to lurk around and make noise. A wedding dress violently shakes and disembodied voices are often heard from the basement. The home is now one of Pennsylvania's many museums.
